header.userPrompt:
Add an AI document-classification gate at document ingestion, before the expensive models run.
Classify each incoming document from its CHEAP local text using JEV (reuse the existing JevClient
from PR #12 — do NOT add Bedrock or any new dependency), then: (a) reject wrong-type documents with
user feedback before the expensive model, (b) persist + log the classification on every document so a
future parser-routing step can use it, (c) flag likely prompt-injection as an advisory signal. This
was validated by an eval (see ~/jev-metadata-eval): on the app's PDFBox text the type classifier is
correct at ~1.0 confidence on real statements and a real Carrefour ticket; it cleanly separates
ticket vs bank_voucher vs invoice; the injection flag catches overt attacks but is only a signal.

=== 1. DocumentClassifier service (server) ===
New service (e.g. net.wiringbits.services.DocumentClassifier) built on JevClient.choose (single
"choice" question per call; JevChoice has choice + confidence + probabilities). It makes TWO cheap
choose calls on the same text:
  - TYPE: criteria keyed by a new enum DocumentClass -> { bank_statement, purchase_ticket,
    bank_voucher, invoice, other }. Criteria descriptions must match the eval wording:
      bank_statement  = a bank or credit-card ACCOUNT STATEMENT listing many transactions over a period
      purchase_ticket = an itemized store PURCHASE TICKET/RECEIPT: products with prices from a shop
      bank_voucher    = a card-payment voucher/slip: amount, bank, card, authorization/TPV, NO items
      invoice         = a factura/invoice/bill (fiscal/billing details, often says FACTURA)
      other           = none of these / unreadable
  - INJECTION (advisory): criteria { clean, injection_attempt } with the eval's instructions
    (text instructing/overriding the AI, revealing its prompt/secrets, or exfiltrating data).
Return a typed result: DocumentClass + confidence (BigDecimal), plus injectionSuspected: Boolean +
its confidence. DocumentClass is a new enumeratum enum (Uppercase entryNames; fail-loud parse on an
unknown value, like the other enums in the codebase).

FAIL-OPEN is mandatory and intentional (this is NOT a silent default for parsed data — call it out in
a comment): if JevConfig.mode is mock, or JEV errors/429s, or the TYPE confidence is below a
configurable threshold, return an "inconclusive" result that callers treat as "do not block; proceed
to the expensive model". Threshold: add `minConfidence` (default 0.85) to the jev config block in
application.conf with an env override; never log the JEV api key.

LOG every classification with the userId in scope (per the coding-patterns reviewer): the chosen
class + confidence and the injection flag + confidence. If injection is suspected, log a WARNING with
the userId (advisory only — never blocks).

=== 2. Persist the classification (evolution) ===
Add nullable columns to persist the result on BOTH ingestion targets, so it is computed ONCE and is
available later for parser routing / feedback even if not yet consumed:
  - document: ai_classification (text, null), ai_classification_confidence (numeric, null),
    ai_injection_suspected (boolean, null), ai_injection_confidence (numeric, null).
  - bank_statement_draft: the same four columns.
New Play evolution, Ups only, following the repo's evolution conventions (no ';' inside comments,
correct hashing). No CHECK constraints. Update the Anorm DAOs/models/parsers for both tables.

=== 3. Statement path gate — ExtractBankStatementDraftAction ===
In ExtractBankStatementDraftAction.apply, the draft's text is already produced by
`PdfTextExtractor.extract(bytes)` right before the slow/paid `extractionService.extract(...)`. Insert
the classifier between them:
  - Classify `text`; persist the result on the draft (columns above).
  - If the class is confidently NOT bank_statement -> call BankStatementDraftRepository.markFailed(
    draftId, reason, now) with a user-facing reason (e.g. "This looks like a <class>, not a bank
    statement."), and SKIP extractionService.extract. The draft UI already surfaces the `error`.
  - bank_statement / inconclusive -> proceed to extraction exactly as today.
Log with the draft's userId.

=== 4. Ticket path gate — ProcessDocumentAction + ParseReceiptAction ===
PRE-TEXTRACT (ProcessDocumentAction.processReceiptOrInvoice, before textractClient.startExpenseAnalysis):
inject BlobStorage, load the document bytes, run PdfTextExtractor.extract:
  - Right(text) (text-layer PDF, e.g. the Carrefour PDF): classify, persist on the document.
      * Confidently NOT purchase_ticket (i.e. bank_voucher / invoice / bank_statement / other) ->
        documentsRepository.updateStatus(doc.id, DocumentStatus.Unsupported, Some(reason)), send the
        Telegram feedback (below), and SKIP Textract (startExpenseAnalysis is NOT called).
      * purchase_ticket or inconclusive -> proceed to Textract exactly as today.
  - Left (image-only/scan — the common Telegram photo case): proceed to Textract as today (there is no
    cheap text to classify yet). Do NOT persist a classification here.
POST-OCR (ParseReceiptAction, where the Textract AnalyzeExpense output is available): if the document
has NO persisted classification yet (the image branch above), classify on the reconstructed Textract
text and persist it — this is the "classify once if not already classified" step. This is ADVISORY
and FAIL-OPEN: do NOT reject or drop a document that already cost a Textract call; still parse it as
today. If it is confidently NOT a purchase_ticket, send the Telegram feedback so the user learns they
sent a voucher/invoice. (Rationale: the pre-Textract gate only SAVES cost on text-layer PDFs; photos
must be OCR'd regardless, so the post-OCR check is for routing + feedback, not cost.)

=== 5. User feedback on rejects ===
  - Statements: the draft `error` reason (set via markFailed) is already shown in the bank-statements
    draft UI — no new UI needed; just set a clear reason string.
  - Tickets (Telegram): on a reject (pre-Textract) or advisory non-ticket (post-OCR), send a message
    via the existing TelegramApi.sendMessage(chatId, ...) to the originating chat. Recover the chatId
    from the document's Telegram linkage (TelegramReceiptRepository / TelegramRepository, as
    TelegramPhotoAction does). If the document did not originate from Telegram, skip the Telegram step
    (do not fail). Message example: "This looks like a <bank voucher/invoice>, not a purchase ticket —
    please send the itemized ticket."

=== EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE ===
No "contains both ticket + voucher" detection. No custom per-class parsers yet (only persist + log the
class for later). No change to the draft->confirm flow, the AiSuggestions feature, the JEV suggestions
engine, or the statement extraction ladder itself.

=== CONSTRAINTS ===
- Follow docs/guide (antipatterns, backend, data-infra, testing, ci-checklist) and CLAUDE.md.
- Reuse JevClient (#12). NO dependency changes (build.sbt/plugins.sbt/package.json); revert incidental
  yarn.lock churn (dependencies reviewer).
- User-scoped DB access (WHERE user_id = ?) on any new/changed query; stable ORDER BY; no CHECK
  constraints; Chimney for case-class mapping; prefer enums over stringly-typed values; never drop a
  Future; log new user-scoped work with the userId after the user is resolved (coding-patterns reviewer).
- The gate is deliberately FAIL-OPEN; this is the one intentional exception to "fail loud" and must be
  commented as such. Everything else still fails loud.
- Evolutions: Ups-only, follow the repo conventions (evolutions reviewer).
- Attribution: do NOT put any Claude session links (claude.ai/ or Claude-Session) in commits or the PR
  description; `Co-Authored-By: Claude` IS allowed.

=== TESTS ===
- DocumentClassifier: TYPE maps each class to its DocumentClass; injection flag parsed; FAIL-OPEN when
  the JevClient is mock / errors / returns below threshold (use a stub JevClient returning a configured
  choice+confidence — do not hit the network).
- Statement path: a non-statement classification marks the draft failed with a reason and does NOT call
  the extraction service; a bank_statement/inconclusive proceeds; the classification is persisted.
- Ticket path pre-Textract: a text-layer non-ticket sets Unsupported + reason, persists the class, and
  does NOT call startExpenseAnalysis; a ticket/inconclusive proceeds to Textract; image-only proceeds
  to Textract with no classification.
- Ticket path post-OCR: classifies only when not already classified (once-guard), persists, is
  fail-open (never drops the document).
- Evolution applies cleanly.
- Verify per task with targeted `sbt "testOnly *Spec"` or `CI=true sbt Test/compile`; the final stage
  runs the full suite.
